name: Flexenpass
kurzbeschreibung: The Flexenpass at 1,773 m connects the Arlberg with the Lechtal: historic pioneering road by Johann Bertolini with natural stone galleries from 1897.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Flexenpass is a history-rich high mountain pass at an altitude of 1,773 meters above sea level in the Austrian federal state of Vorarlberg, in immediate proximity to the Tyrolean Arlberg and Lechtal regions. Nestled between the Lechquellengebirge mountains to the west and the rugged ridges of the Lechtaler Alpen to the east, the pass connects the Klostertal valley (Stuben am Arlberg) with the high-altitude Lechtal and the world-renowned resort destinations of Zürs and Lech am Arlberg. Owing to its key geographical location, the Flexenpass represents the year-round lifeline for the high alpine valleys of the Arlberg.

History & Engineering

For centuries, crossing the Flexenpass was a life-threatening undertaking. The old bridle path traversed precipitous rock faces and was routinely buried in winter by massive avalanches descending from the slopes of the Flexenkrumbach valley, leaving Lech and Zürs cut off from the outside world for weeks. Following the opening of the Arlberg Railway in 1884, the need for a secure road connection surged dramatically. Based on plans drawn up by state building officer Paul Ilmer, construction of the daring Flexenstraße commenced on August 3, 1895. The formidable execution of the project was entrusted to the legendary master builder Johann (Giovanni) Bertolini from the Bregenzerwald. Under the most extreme alpine conditions, Bertolini and hundreds of workers carved the roadway directly into vertical cliff walls. They erected masterful avalanche protection galleries constructed from native natural stone, bridges, and open arched arcades that gave the road its world-famous appearance. On October 11, 1897, the first section up to the pass summit was ceremonially inaugurated. For its 125th anniversary, Bertolini was commemorated in Stuben with a bronze memorial plaque.

Visit & Getting There

The Flexenpass road (B198) is open year-round and completely toll-free (no special toll, no vignette required on the state highway). Because the connecting road between Lech and Warth is routinely closed in winter for safety reasons, the Flexenpass serves as the sole drivable road connection to Zürs and Lech during the snow-rich months. Temporary road closures may occur during extreme snowfalls or controlled avalanche blasting (check current traffic updates via ÖAMTC). Getting there by car: from the east/Tyrol via the Arlberg expressway S16 or the toll-free B197 via Stuben, branching off onto the B198 up through the galleries to the Flexenpass. By public transport: by train (ÖBB) to Langen am Arlberg station, from where bus lines 750 and 760 operate at regular intervals via Stuben and the Flexenpass to Zürs and Lech.

Tips

Driving through the heritage-protected natural stone arcades reveals breathtaking downward views into the wild Flexenschlucht gorge. Safe lay-bys near the pass summit provide spectacular photo stops (please mind the flowing traffic). At the pass summit, the historic Flexenhütte mountain hut invites travelers in for refreshments. For hikers, the pass serves as an ideal trailhead for alpine hikes to the Trittkopfbahn or along the long-distance Lechweg trail toward the Lechquellengebirge.
